title: Wayne State men's basketball falls to Findlay in final non-conference matchup
text:
Bryan Smothers Head Coach | Wayne State University Athletics Website
Bryan Smothers Head Coach | Wayne State University Athletics Website
The Wayne State University men's basketball team lost its final non-conference game of the season, falling 95-81 to the University of Findlay on Tuesday night in Findlay, Ohio. The loss brings Wayne State's record to 2-2 as they prepare for the start of league play next week.
The first half was marked by several lead changes early on. Wayne State briefly led 11-10 following a basket from senior Carlos Paul III, but Findlay responded with an eight-point run and maintained control for the rest of the half. By halftime, Findlay had built a 53-33 lead, aided by shooting 61 percent from the field and capitalizing on Wayne State’s turnovers.
Paul led Wayne State in the first half with 10 points. Jake Bishop contributed 10 points off the bench for Findlay.
In the second half, Wayne State outscored Findlay 48-42 and narrowed their deficit to eight points at one stage after a basket by Jotham Nweke. However, Findlay secured its win by making all ten of its final points from free throws.
Wayne State shot 44 percent from the field and made seven three-pointers out of eighteen attempts. The Oilers converted over half their shots and were particularly effective from beyond the arc, making fourteen threes. Both teams finished with fifteen turnovers each, while rebounding was nearly even.
Redshirt freshman JaKobie Boose scored a career-high 18 points for Wayne State. Junior guard Jordan Briggs led all scorers with 20 points. Paul added another 18 points along with eight rebounds, while Nweke also collected eight boards.
Findlay’s Steele Meister recorded a team-high nineteen points and tied Mason Brandt for most rebounds on his team with six each.
Wayne State will begin GLIAC conference play next week when it visits Purdue Northwest on Tuesday before hosting Ferris State on Saturday afternoon.
